header.name: Mobile & Ubiquitous Computing
header.description: The course offers a comprehensive introduction to Mobile and Ubiquitous Computing, enabling students to understand the seamless integration of computing capabilities into everyday objects and mobile platforms. It prepares and trains students to program mobile devices with an understanding of the constraints and opportunities that mobile systems offer. The course focuses on the fundamental principles, methodologies, and applications that drive intelligent, connected, and context-aware systems. Students will learn how mobile and ubiquitous systems can sense, process, and respond intelligently to user contexts, enabling adaptive and personalized experiences. Through hands-on activities, assignments, and case studies, students will gain familiarity with sensors, assistive system design, data collection and visualization, and affective computing. The course emphasizes both the technical and human-centered aspects of designing mobile and ubiquitous systems that interact seamlessly with users and their surroundings.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be introduced to the basics and concepts of Mobile and Ubiquitous Computing. They will be able to comprehend and identify its emergence, context and importance in the society.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to understand the scope, resources, modalities and explain the techniques of Mobile and Ubiquitous Computing.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to apply the knowledge of Mobile and Ubiquitous Computing techniques, modalities and processes to applications and generate research ideas.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students will be able to critically evaluate existing Mobile and Ubiquitous Computing-based design solutions, propose alternate approaches, and integrate responsible and ethical design principles into their work.
